metadata.case_name: CHIU AH TUNG v. TANG CHUNG CHUEN AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_before: managing a joint venture business named Shenzhen Natural Cosmetic Beauty Co. Ltd.

injuries.description: posterior dislocation of the left hip associated with fracture of the posterior lip of the acetabulum and the antero-inferior part of the femoral head.
source: The plaintiff suffered from a posterior dislocation of the left hip associated with fracture of the posterior lip of the acetabulum and the antero-inferior part of the femoral head.
injuries.icd_description: Multiple injuries of hip or thigh

injuries.description: an undisplaced crack fracture at the neck of the right humerus.
source: There was also an undisplaced crack fracture at the neck of the right humerus.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of surgical neck of humerus

manifestations.description: not able to travel in and out of Hong Kong to the Mainland and to various parts of the Mainland with the same agility as before

treatments_received.treatment: closed reduction of the hip dislocation and insertion of Steinmenn pin into the left proximal tibia to facilitate skeletal traction
source: The first one on 26 November 1998 for closed reduction of the hip dislocation and insertion of Steinmenn pin into the left proximal tibia to facilitate skeletal traction.

treatments_received.treatment: open reduction and internal fixation of the acetabular hip fracture and excision of the femoral head fragment
source: The second one on 1 December 1998 for open reduction and internal fixation of the acetabular hip fracture and excision of the femoral head fragment.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Closed / open reduction of fracture of acetabulum with internal fixation

treatments_received.treatment: Medical expenses for in-patient, out-patient, acupuncture, bonesetter and herbal medicine
source: Medical expenses for in-patient, out-patient, acupuncture, bonesetter and herbal medicine $8,746

losses.description: physical handicap; not able to travel in and out of Hong Kong to the Mainland and to various parts of the Mainland with the same agility as before
